Python Console

Run your own Python over curated, read-only fleet datasets inside a locked-down sandbox — for one-off reports and checks that no built-in page answers.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsstudio.python_console audit.view
📍 WhereAdministrator → Studio → Python Studio → Console, in every ADOM (URL /studio/?pane=console); also the Console tab of every script's editor

What is it?#

ℹ️Note

Now part of Python Studio. The console and the Script Library share one page, Administrator → Studio → Python Studio: the Console pane is this tool, and every script's editor has a Console tab with it too. The old address /database/py-console opens the Console pane.

The Python Console runs a Python script you write against a snapshot of selected SATOM datasets — appliances, cached server policies, pools, WAF profiles, certificates, recent audit activity and so on. The script runs in an isolated sandbox: it can read only the data you ticked, cannot reach the network, the database or SATOM's secrets, and is stopped after a few seconds. It is meant for quick reports and data checks.

What does it do?#

  • Lets you tick one or more datasets; each becomes data['<key>'], a dictionary with columns and rows (a list of dictionaries).
  • Runs the script and shows Output (stdout) and Errors (stderr), a status badge (ok, timed out or exit N / exit killed), the duration and the datasets used.
  • Offers Browse examples — a catalogue of ready-made scripts grouped by topic (fleet, certificates, audit activity, cross-references, data-quality checks…). Inserting an example also ticks the datasets it needs.

Datasets#

Key Contents
fleet_appliances The managed devices visible to you: name, kind, firmware, host, port
server_policies Cached FortiWeb server policies with their key columns
server_policies_full Cached server policies with traffic log, web protection profile, monitor mode, comment and the App ID parsed from the comment
server_pools Cached back-end pools with type and protocol
web_protection_profiles Cached WAF profiles with their signature and bot-mitigation references
certificates Certificates tracked by the Certificate Manager (no key material)
audit_recent The 200 most recent audit-log rows; empty if you lack audit.view
fleet_counts One row: device, server-policy and certificate totals
scheduled_actions Configured scheduled actions: name, action, next run

These are the same datasets Plugin Studio uses. They return only rows of the devices visible to you in the current ADOM (devices in maintenance stay hidden unless your profile may see them).

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: datasets now contain only rows of the devices visible to you, audit_recent is empty without audit.view, and the menu entries follow studio.python_console (the Global Studio group is no longer inside Administrator).

ℹ️Note

Changed in 3.1.0: in the Global ADOM, Studio is a sub-menu at the foot of Administrator again; a profile without users.manage keeps the standalone Studio group. Every device ADOM, not only FortiADC, lists Administrator → Python Console.

Limits#

The console runs inside the web service, so it is bounded tightly: nothing in the jail is writable (no /tmp, read-only root and /dev — a file in a memory filesystem is memory no per-process limit counts), 512 MiB per process, a few processes or threads beyond those that exist, the output read as it arrives and kept up to 200 KB per stream, and one run at a time per node (a second one is told the console is busy).

Requirements#

  • The bwrap (bubblewrap) program must be installed on the SATOM node. Without it every run returns sandbox unavailable: bubblewrap (bwrap) is not installed.
  • A python3 interpreter under /usr on the node (the sandbox runs /usr/bin/python3).

Permissions#

Action Needs
Open the console and run scripts studio.python_console

studio.python_console is an admin-only permission; only the seeded admin profile includes it. Users without it do not get the Console pane of Python Studio nor the editor's Console tab, and the console's run endpoint (/studio/console/run) answers 403 — even for a holder of studio.script_library, who opens Python Studio on the Scripts pane only.

In the Global ADOM Python Studio is under Administrator → Studio. A profile that holds studio.python_console (or another Studio permission) but not users.manage cannot see Administrator and gets a standalone Studio group instead. In every device ADOM, Administrator → Studio → Python Studio is listed for holders of either Python Studio permission; it has no fallback there, because the Administrator group needs users.manage.

How to use#

  1. Open Administrator → Studio → Python Studio (or Studio → Python Studio if your profile has no Administrator group) and click Console in the Explorer on the left.
  2. In Data bundle, tick the datasets your script needs.
  3. Write the script in Script, or click Browse examples and insert one.
  4. Click Run. The status shows Running in sandbox… and then the result.
  5. Read Output (stdout); if the script failed, Errors (stderr) shows the traceback (the sandbox's own frames are hidden).

Configuration#

Item Value
Script size Up to 100,000 characters
Wall-clock limit 8 seconds per run
Memory 1 GiB address space
Processes 256
Largest file the script may write (in its scratch /tmp) 16 MiB
Open files 128
Captured output 200,000 characters each for stdout and stderr
Rows per dataset Up to 1,000

Example#

🧪Example — Policies without a WAF profile

Tick server_policies_full and run:

rows = data['server_policies_full']['rows']
missing = [r for r in rows if not r.get('wpp')]
print(f"{len(missing)} of {len(rows)} policies have NO WAF profile")
for r in missing:
    print(' -', r['device'], '/', r['policy'])

Result#

  • Nothing is written anywhere: the script receives a read-only JSON copy of the data, and its scratch space is discarded after the run.
  • Every run is written to the audit log as py_console.run, including the datasets, whether it succeeded, the exit code, whether it timed out, the duration and the first 1,000 characters of the source. See Audit log.

Troubleshooting#

"sandbox unavailable: bubblewrap (bwrap) is not installed"#

Possible causes - The bwrap package is missing on this SATOM node.

Solution 1. Install bubblewrap on the node (an operating-system package), then run again.

Verification - A trivial script such as print('ok') returns the ok badge.

The badge says "timed out"#

Possible causes - The script ran longer than 8 seconds (or exhausted its CPU allowance).

Solution 1. Tick fewer datasets, or avoid nested loops over large row lists.

KeyError on data['…']#

Possible causes - The dataset was not ticked, so it is not in the bundle.

Solution 1. Tick it in Data bundle and run again.

A dataset is empty and has an "error" key#

Possible causes - The underlying table does not exist on this installation, or the query failed. The error text is in data['<key>']['error'].

A dataset has no rows#

Possible causes - audit_recent is empty for users without audit.view. - None of the rows belong to a device visible to you (another ADOM, or in maintenance).

Some values read as masked#

Possible causes - Columns whose names contain password, secret, token, _enc, fernet or private are masked by the read-only query layer.

Advanced#

Advanced The sandbox

Each run starts a fresh bubblewrap jail: all namespaces unshared (so no network), the environment cleared (SATOM's keys and database address are not visible), only /usr, /proc, /dev and an empty /tmp mounted, and the script plus its data bundle bound read-only at /sandbox. The application directory, its configuration file and the database are not mounted. Resource limits are applied with prlimit and the run is killed with timeout.

Advanced Risks to keep in mind
  • Data exposure inside the output. The console cannot write or reach the network, but anything it prints is shown to the person running it — including host names and addresses of the appliances visible to that person and, with audit.view, the latest audit entries.
  • Audit trail holds code. The first 1,000 characters of every script are copied into the audit log; do not paste credentials into a script.
  • Resource use. Each run spawns a process on the SATOM node; limits keep a single run small, but runs are not queued or rate-limited.
